bracket: [Textbook answer-key error: the printed answer is \(1.56\,\text{V}\); for the reaction as written it is \(1.10\,\text{V}\). The key's value is reproduced EXACTLY by a nameable substitution — Table 2.1 prints \(E^{\circ}(\text{Ag}^{+}/\text{Ag}) = 0.80\,\text{V}\) and \(E^{\circ}(\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}) = -0.76\,\text{V}\), and \(0.80 - (-0.76) = 1.56\) to the digit — but \(\text{Ag}^{+}\) appears nowhere in this reaction, whose cathode couple is \(\text{Ag}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Ag} + 2\text{OH}^-\) at \(+0.342\,\text{V}\), giving \(0.342 - (-0.762) = 1.104\,\text{V}\). Nor is \(1.56\) the real silver-oxide button cell's voltage, which is about \(1.60\,\text{V}\) and arises from an alkaline \(\text{Zn}/\text{ZnO}\) anode that would contradict the stem's own \(\text{Zn}^{2+}(aq)\) product — so that reading does not rescue it either. There is a second, milder defect behind this one worth knowing: **the \(\text{Ag}_2\text{O}/\text{Ag}\) couple is absent from Table 2.1**, so the chapter supplies no data for its own cathode and a student working strictly from the book cannot reach \(1.104\,\text{V}\) unaided. That is very likely how the key came to use the only silver couple the table does provide.]
